title: Adic stratified finite presentations and finite constant local models
statement: Fix a universe $u$ and a prime $\ell$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme in universe $u$, meaning quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate] of one of the three families $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite. For the algebraic closure use the finite-subextension-valued ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and $D_X=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Under the section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], a $\Lambda_X$-module $M$ is constructible in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense [def-sfb-constructible-module] if and only if it is constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification $X=\coprod_aX_a$ and on every stratum a pro-étale cover $\{U_{ai}\to X_a\}$ and finitely presented scalar $\Lambda(*)$-modules $P_{ai}$ with $M|_{U_{ai}}\cong\Lambda_{U_{ai}}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_{ai}$. The stratifications on the two sides may differ, and integral torsion scalar modules are allowed. Consequently the bounded constructible full subcategory $\mathcal B_X$ of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] equals $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], as object properties in the same ordinary derived category $D_X$. No derived-completeness condition is imposed.

source.place: Part (2), integral/rational bullets: comparison of the stratified local-presentation and finite constant local-model predicates; extracted from the returned item, step 2. The complete short agent proof with cited nodes is in report.md, under Proof in words for this node.

proof.text: Both predicates are stated in the same internal module category. Reuse the proved comparison_of_local_models helper from the integral comparison module. For the converse it pulls back a finite scalar presentation, transports it along the canonical coefficient isomorphism, and retains the stratification. For the forward direction it uses local Noetherianity and compactness to make X qcqs, and the embedding of each stratum into the Noetherian underlying space makes the stratum Noetherian. It transports local finite presentation to the canonical condensed coefficient ring before applying a coefficient-specific local-model theorem. Retain the Cartesian-coefficient module prescribed by the unit route; its canonical comparison is the coefficient identification used throughout.

Apply the integral comparison after identifying its coefficients with the certified embedded integers. Lift the finite field E to ULift E in the scheme universe. The spectral extension absolute value equals its extension norm. The ring equivalence from its WithAbs valuation ring to the embedded integers is therefore an isometry in both directions. Postcomposition gives mutually inverse morphisms of continuous-function condensed rings, compatible with multiplication. Restriction of scalars along the resulting coefficient isomorphism transports both module predicates: it preserves regular modules, finite sums and cokernel presentations, and commutes with restriction to strata and the point. Applying the inverse recovers the original module. Thus integralLfpConstantModelComparison supplies the integral branch, including torsion.

For a finite normed field E use ULift E to match the universe of the field local-triviality theorem. Down and up are continuous inverse ring homomorphisms, hence identify the continuous condensed coefficient rings. On a Noetherian stratum apply exists_finiteFree_cover_of_condensedField_lfp. Transport its free module along the canonical coefficient isomorphism to obtain finite free canonical restrictions. A rank-n free module is the pullback of the rank-n free module over the condensed point ring: mapMod preserves regular modules and finite biproducts. The point module is finitely presented as the cokernel of a zero endomorphism. This gives the required finite constant local models and the stratified predicate; transport across the coefficient isomorphism as above.

For the certified finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure ring apply condensedQbar_lfp_locally_free on each Noetherian stratum. Its canonical coefficient restrictions already have the desired free isomorphisms. Use the same rank-n point module and zero-matrix presentation to obtain finite constant local models. This uses the specified coefficient ring without replacing it by all continuous functions into the algebraic closure.

Eliminate the three constructors of the coefficient certificate and combine the preceding module comparisons. The ordinary derived bounded-constructible predicates have literally the same t-structure boundedness factor. Substitute the module-predicate equivalence in each integer cohomological degree and apply propositional and function extensionality. No completeness condition is introduced.
